one_liner: Rust GPU rasterizer for glyphs and vector paths (OpenGL, Metal, WebGL 2); claims to match or beat CPU rasterizers, with no numbers.
what_it_does: A workspace of pathfinder_* crates. You build a scene of paths and text through pathfinder_canvas, a subset of the HTML Canvas 2D API, or load SVG through resvg/usvg, and render it straight into a GPU framebuffer with OpenGL 3.0+/ES 3.0+, WebGL 2 or Metal. Text goes through pathfinder_text, which gets glyph outlines from font-kit and runs layout through skribo (HarfBuzz), so shaping is delegated and Pathfinder rasterizes glyphs as paths. A C API (static library built with cargo-c, header generated by cbindgen) covers canvas, paths, fill/stroke/measure text, SVG scenes and the GL and Metal renderers. It is not a FreeType-style bitmap API.
how_it_is_fast: Paths are cut into 16x16 tiles. Tiles that are entirely one solid colour are flagged, and tiles hidden behind them are culled before any GPU work, which avoids the overdraw of painter's-algorithm software renderers. Edges are rasterized into a 16-bit float coverage mask with exact trapezoidal area coverage (described as effectively 256xAA), and tiles are then shaded back to front from that mask. At the 'D3D9' level (OpenGL 3/WebGL 2) binning and tiling run on the CPU with SIMD (pathfinder_simd) and Rayon, pipelined with the GPU. At the 'D3D11' level (OpenGL 4.3, Metal) bin, fill and composite all run in GPU compute shaders. Because GPU fill parallelises across pixels while CPU rasterizer cost grows with pixel area, the claimed advantage is largest at large glyph sizes.
when_to_use: Rust apps, or C/C++ apps willing to link a Rust static library, that already render with OpenGL or Metal and draw large, zoomed or per-frame-transformed text and vector paths, where CPU rasterize-and-upload is the bottleneck.
Complex SVG- or PDF-like scenes with heavy overlap, where tile occlusion culling skips hidden geometry.
Text placed in 3D or VR scenes, or animated in size, where a glyph-atlas cache from a CPU rasterizer keeps getting invalidated.
As a readable reference design for tiled GPU vector rendering with exact area coverage.
when_not_to_use: You need CPU bitmaps or a glyph atlas (headless servers, no GPU, software fallback): use FreeType, fontdue or font-rs. Reading pixels back from the GPU gives up the advantage.
You need shaping or line layout: Pathfinder delegates that to skribo/HarfBuzz, and the record's category fit is approximate.

You want a stable, versioned dependency: the crates.io releases of pathfinder_canvas, pathfinder_renderer and pathfinder_text are still 0.5.0 from 2020-04-17, and that pathfinder_renderer has no D3D11 compute mode at all (checked in the 0.5.0 crate source), so the compute path the README highlights needs a git dependency on main. The README itself says 'under heavy development and is incomplete'.

C or C++ projects that want a native library: the C bindings are 'less complete' (README), produce a static library only, need a Rust toolchain plus cargo-c, and pin old dependencies (font-kit 0.6, usvg 0.9).
Small UI text on low-end hardware, where the README itself only claims to 'often match' CPU rasterizers, or CPUs without SSE4.1 (see gotchas).

integration.form: crate (modular pathfinder_* Rust crates); static lib with a C API via cargo-c
integration.dependencies: rayon, font-kit, skribo (HarfBuzz), usvg/resvg for SVG, gl or metal bindings, half, hashbrown and others; C build needs cargo-c
integration.min_toolchain: not documented; Rust 2018 edition, CI builds on stable Rust; no rust-version declared on crates.io
integration.platforms: Needs a GPU: OpenGL 3.0+/ES 3.0+, WebGL 2 or Metal ('D3D9' level, CPU binning); compute 'D3D11' level needs OpenGL 4.3 or Metal. CPU side: x86-64 (SIMD paths assume SSE4.1) and aarch64 (CI cross-builds the simd and geometry crates)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; scene building runs on a Rayon executor (SceneProxy), and rendering is tied to the caller's GL or Metal context

gotchas: pathfinder_simd calls SSE4.1 intrinsics (_mm_floor_ps, _mm_ceil_ps, _mm_min_epi32, _mm_max_epi32, _mm_mullo_epi32) from safe APIs without a target-feature check, so pre-SSE4.1 x86 CPUs hit undefined behaviour or illegal-instruction crashes. Issues #502 (2022) and #588 (May 2026) are open with no fix.

Which level you get is decided per device (RendererLevel::default_for_device): on WebGL 2 and other GL 3.x devices, tiling stays on the CPU, so very complex scenes can be CPU-bound (issue #228, 'High CPU overhead on very complex scenes').
crates.io 0.5.0 (2020) and git main differ substantially (no compute mode in 0.5.0), so examples and docs on main may not match the published crates.
Font hinting is limited to 'slight' hinting, and stem darkening is optional, so small-size output will not match FreeType's full hinting.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The other entries in this category are CPU glyph rasterizers (font-rs, fontdue, TiTanF) or, in msdfgl's case, GPU atlas generators. Pick Pathfinder only when glyphs are drawn directly on the GPU at large or changing sizes and transforms. Pick fontdue or font-rs for CPU bitmaps and atlases at UI sizes, and msdfgl for scalable atlas-based text. For general GPU vector rendering, Vello (rasterizers-2d) is the actively developed compute renderer with third-party measurements.
verified_claims_summary: There is no measurement against any baseline. The README claims Pathfinder 'often matches or exceeds' unnamed 'best CPU rasterizers', with 'multi-factor speedups' at large sizes. doc/architecture.md quotes only absolute Pathfinder 3 stage times for the Ghostscript tiger at 1600x1600 on an i7-7920HQ with Intel HD Graphics 630 (about 2.2 ms CPU tile/cull/pack, 2.6 ms GPU fill, 2.3 ms GPU shade). An independent 2019 write-up by Mozilla's Nicolas Silva says only that it is 'a good deal faster at rendering very large and complex SVG drawings than using a CPU rasterizer and uploading the result to a texture', also without numbers, so tier D stands.
measurement_notes: There is no benchmark harness to audit. The demo (demo/common/src/lib.rs) has a stats overlay showing CPU/GPU frame times, but no benchmark mode and no baseline renderer. Correction to the verifier: doc/architecture.md does carry numbers, absolute per-stage timings for the tiger at 1600x1600 on an i7-7920HQ with HD 630, written for the CPU-tiling pipeline, but no comparison, so tier D is unaffected. The only third-party source found, nical.github.io/posts/a-look-at-pathfinder.html (2019-05-28, read via raw.githubusercontent.com/nical/nical.github.io), is qualitative. The 2017 Pathfinder 1 post with FreeType, stb_truetype and font-rs charts is for a different algorithm and stays blocked. No correctness bug sits behind any catalogued number, because there are none. Separately, open issues #502 and #588 document SSE4.1 undefined behaviour in pathfinder_simd.
record_corrections: (1) doc/architecture.md is not number-free: it gives absolute stage timings without a baseline (see measurement_notes). (2) The crates.io releases of the renderer, canvas and text crates are 0.5.0 from 2020-04-17, without the compute mode. Ongoing activity is mostly pathfinder_simd maintenance: 0.5.6 was published 2026-04-23, the same day as the last commit, and that crate has about 20.3M downloads as a font-kit-family dependency. (3) Category: a GPU glyph and vector rasterizer fits rasterizers-2d (with Vello, Blaze, Blend2D and vger) better than font-shaping-text-layout. (4) The repo shows 97 open issues and 24 open PRs.
status_note: The repo is technically active (last commit 2026-04-23), but the activity is SIMD and build upkeep: the renderer has had no release since 0.5.0 in 2020, and the README still says it is under heavy development. MIT OR Apache-2.0 makes it easy to adopt from git main, but plan to own your fork.
